our solution enables end hosts to steer flows over any desired path in a network without relying on packet header extensions, and that our method can improve the performance of MultiPath TCP when combined with an elephant flow scheduling system in large data center network.

the development of new load-balancing techniques that enable end hosts to select the forwarding path for a specific flow in data center networks without the need to modify routers or introduce any additional packet headers.
the design and implementation of a deterministic flow-based path selection method that is stateless in the network and allows to steer the flow of packets over any desired load balanced path.
a simple and efficient way to deterministically steer flows over any desired path without requiring packet header extensions.

we have developed a deterministic path selection technique which is stateless, efficient and can be used with any transport-level protocol, such as TCP or QUIC.
our solution allows for a stateless deterministic load-balancing method in the context of data center networking.

a deterministic path selection is feasible in data center networks, even without any header extension.
